newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Opposition set to form next Romanian government.
newsitem.headline: Opposition set to form next Romanian government.

text.p: Romania's opposition soundly won Sunday's parliamentary elections and should be able to form a government, breaking a seven-year stranglehold on power by ex-Communists under President Ion Iliescu, exit polls showed.

Both state and private television surveys showed the Democratic Convention bloc led by Emil Constantinescu well ahead on around 35 percent, pushing the scandal-ridden leftist Party of Social Democracy down to some 25 percent support.
If the results of the exit polls are confirmed by official results, which should begin to trickle in late on Monday, it will mark a sea-change in the Romanian political scene.
Romania is the only eastern European country where the anti-communist opposition has not yet had a spell in power.

Constantinescu welcomed the polls, greeted ecstatically by supporters at his headquarters, but cautioned his followers to wait for the official count and brace themselves for tough coalition bargaining ahead.

The CDR will need the support of ex-premier Petre Roman's Social Democratic party and either liberal or Hungarian minority groups. Iliescu, if he wins the presidential race, faces working with a hostile assembly demanding policy change.
